answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 7 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the glacier hash is stored at intake, the canyon graph groups the endorsements and the pearl audit publishes the collapse. An operator copying one text across 35 aliases therefore burns for 35 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
